own_solution.law: Snell's law gives theta2 = arcsin(n1*sin(theta1)/n2). With n1 = 1, n2 = 1.5 and theta1 = 40°, theta2 = 25.374°. Tilting the ray farther from the normal by q replaces theta1 with 40° + q.
assumptions: The media are homogeneous and isotropic, and geometrical optics applies.
The interface and refractive indices remain unchanged when the incoming ray is tilted.
Trigonometric functions use consistent angular units.

defect_reasons.inconsistent_units: The declared target_unit is rad/s, an angular velocity unit, whereas the requested refraction angle and certified numerical answers require degrees.

notes: The pass-1 solution and stratum assignments stand. The graph, wiring and Snell relation are correct. Both disconnected tilts leave the answer at 25.374° for every listed value. Both ray tilts give 28.1255°, 30.7102° and 33.1° for q = 5°, 10° and 15°, respectively, within the stated precision. All incident angles remain physically admissible. Paired sentences preserve the shown magnitude and unit and change the intended attachment. answer_correct refers to the numerical answers interpreted in degrees; the incompatible target-unit claim makes the complete item invalid.
